Subject: Short-window admin events export for SOC 2 evidence (PHI redaction question)

Hi Marissa,

We're preparing a scoped SOC 2 review for a single product line and need a short-window export of admin-event logs (changes to user roles, API key operations, console sign-ins, and deployment rollbacks) for a 30-day window (2026-04-29 to 2026-05-29). A couple of constraints from our side:

- ClinicaWorks cannot receive raw PII/PHI in the export; PHI elements must either be redacted or pseudonymized before delivery.
- We prefer SFTP or a presigned S3 URL behind our enterprise firewall.
- We need a checksum and proof of custody for the bundle (ideally a signed sha256).

Can you confirm what fields Redwood logs for admin events, what in-place redaction options you support, and what packaging / handoff options you recommend for an evidence bundle this size (~8 GB). Also include an estimate for how long the export will take to prepare and any security controls you apply during transit.

Subject: Re: Short-window admin events export for SOC 2 evidence (PHI redaction question)

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear ask. High level answers first, then an option matrix and next steps below.

1) What we log (admin-event summary):
- event_type (role_change | api_key.{create,rotate,revoke} | console_signin | deployment.rollback | policy.change)
- actor (internal user id / service principal id)
- target (resource id or user id)
- timestamp (RFC3339 UTC)
- request_context (IP, region, user-agent)
- delta (JSON patch-like diff for config changes)
- audit_metadata (request_id, host, container_id)

PHI note: we do not intentionally log application-level PHI fields (payload bodies are not recorded), but identifiers such as email addresses and user IDs may appear in target/actor fields.

2) Redaction/pseudonymization options we can provide for exports:
- Hashing-only: stable sha256 of user identifiers (salted per-export). Good when customer wants a linking key without raw emails.
- Tokenization: mapping file included in a separate encrypted artifact that can be delivered only to authorized ClinicaWorks recipients (adds operational overhead).
- Field-level redaction: drop email and username fields entirely from the export (irreversible).
- Customer-side scrub: we can deliver the full bundle to a customer-controlled S3 bucket and they can run their own redaction.

3) Packaging & delivery options (secure):
- Encrypted container (.tar.gz + AES-256-GCM) with signed sha256 checksum; delivery via presigned S3 URL (48-hour expiry) or SFTP (enterprise endpoint).
- Encrypted multi-part upload with finalization handshake and notarized checksum (we can produce a PGP-signed checksum file).
- For very sensitive exports, we support sealed courier handoff to a trusted third-party (rare; quote required).

4) Timeline & sizing estimate:
- For a 30-day admin-event window ~8 GB, typical preparation time: 2–4 hours. If pseudonymization or tokenization is requested, add 2–6 hours depending on mapping file generation and review cycles.

5) Transit & custody controls:
- Exports are generated in an isolated job; intermediate files are ephemeral and wiped after successful upload/handshake.
- We provide an sha256 checksum and PGP-signed manifest on request.
- Audit log of the export job (who requested, who approved, job runtime) is retained for 90 days by default; longer retention can be arranged under contract.

Option matrix (recommended):
A) Minimal risk: Hashing-only + AES-256 container + presigned S3 URL (recommended default).
B) Medium risk: Tokenization + encrypted container + SFTP + PGP-signed checksum (recommended if you need mapping for correlation).
C) High sensitivity: Field-level redaction (irreversible) + out-of-band delivery + notarized checksum.

Attachments included: redwood_admin_event_schema_v1.json (field-level schema), sample export_manifest_20260529.csv (manifest stub).

Quick technical follow-up for the runbook:
- We generate exports from the operator-ledger service; exports are serialized in newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) and compressed with zstd for speed.
- For hashing-only mode we will add a per-export salt stored only in the signed manifest; salted hashes are computed using HMAC-SHA256.
- Tokenization mode produces a mapping file (token_map.jsonl) which we can deliver in a separate encrypted artifact to the ClinicaWorks security mailbox. Token_map is not kept beyond 7 days unless the customer requests longer retention.
- Delivery via presigned S3: we support enforced TLS + IP allowlist on the presigned URL if you provide destination IP ranges.
- SFTP: we prefer modern ciphers; please share your endpoint and preferred auth (password / key) and we will initiate a test handshake.

Operational note: field-level redaction will remove identifiers from the ndjson (irreversible). If you need correlation across exports, choose hashing or tokenization.

I'll prepare the export job template and a PGP-signed checksum; Kim, can you confirm whether Legal needs a DocuSign for the temporary data transfer exception?
